summary: Function: runs multi-line JavaScript; `Inputs.x` mints the port `in-x`, `Outputs.y` the port `out-y` — wire the prefixed name.
description: The Function node executes the JavaScript in `functionScript`. The script's surface *is* its port list, but the connectable port **name** is prefixed and the script name is not: reading `Inputs.name` creates an input port called **`in-name`**, assigning `Outputs.name = value` creates a value output called **`out-name`**, and calling `Outputs.name()` creates and fires a signal output called **`out-name`** (conventionally `Outputs.Success()` / `Outputs.Failure()`). The property panel labels each of these with its unprefixed display name, so what you read on the node (`name`) is not what a connection must be written to (`in-name`) — wire to the prefixed name. The node's own static ports (`run`, `done`, `success`, `failure`, `completed`, `unchanged`, `error`) are never prefixed, which is exactly why the prefix exists: a script calling `Outputs.done()` gets `out-done`, distinct from the built-in `done`. The script runs whenever a ticked input changes, and additionally when the `run` signal fires — connecting `run` takes nothing away; untick an input under Run On Value Change to stop that one triggering a run. A `run` you triggered reports `done` once the script has finished (awaiting an async body first), `failure` if it threw or would not compile, and `unchanged` when there is no script written yet. Scripts may be async and use `await` — fire a signal output when done to sequence downstream work. To share code between Functions, put it in a script file in the project (`scripts/<name>.js`) and list the file under **Uses** on each Function that needs it. The file gives what it assigns to `exports` (`exports.canStep = function (tile) { … }`), and a Function calls it as `Scripts.<file name>.canStep(tile)`. Fix the file once and every Function that uses it runs the new code.
whenToUse: Anything beyond a one-liner: data transformation, calling browser APIs or fetch, orchestrating async steps. Prefer Expression for simple pure computations and dedicated nodes (Query Records, REST2) where they exist — graphs stay more inspectable than scripts.

ports.functionScript: The JavaScript source. Its Inputs./Outputs. references define the node's data and signal ports — `Inputs.x` mints the port named `in-x`, `Outputs.y` the port named `out-y`, each displayed under its bare name.
ports.run: Signal; executes the script. When connected, input changes no longer auto-run the script.
ports.scriptInputs: Editor-managed list of the input ports the script declares — not authored directly.
ports.scriptOutputs: Editor-managed list of the output ports the script declares — not authored directly.
ports.uses: This lists the project's script files that the Function uses, by their path inside `scripts/` (`engine/world.js`). The code reaches each one as `Scripts.<file name>`, so `engine/world.js` is `Scripts.world`. It's edit-only and takes no wire.

runtimeBehavior: All data/signal ports are runtime-discovered from the script source: the parser (JavascriptNodeParser) mines `Inputs.x` / `Outputs.y` references and registers a port whose `name` is `in-x` / `out-y` and whose `displayName` is the bare `x` / `y`. An authoring tool must write the script first and then wire to the **prefixed** names — `toProperty: "in-x"`, `fromProperty: "out-y"` — never to the bare name the script uses, which is a display label only. Signal outputs follow the same rule and are the calls (`Outputs.y()`), not the assignments. A connection written to the bare name is accepted by every write path and every static validator (this type's ports are runtime-discovered, so the port-existence gate deliberately does not fire) and then fails on the canvas as "Target port doesn't exist". The node's own static ports — `run`, `done`, `success`, `failure`, `completed`, `unchanged`, `error` — are declared, not mined, and are wired unprefixed. The Script node (`Javascript2`) declares its ports and does not prefix them; the two conventions differ. Script files: each file in `uses` is compiled once per app run, however many Functions use it. The body is given a fifth argument, `Scripts`. Inside a file, `use('engine/words')` reaches another file. A file gives values out through CommonJS's `exports` or `module.exports`. `Noodl`, `window` and `document` are `undefined` inside a file, so it runs the same in the browser, in a server render and in an export. Work that touches the app stays in the Function. A file never mints a port. If a used file is missing or fails, the Function stops before any of its body runs. The error is raised once, naming the file and every Function that uses it. In a cloud function a Function with Uses is refused: "Script files don't run in cloud functions yet". Editing a file re-runs the Functions that use it in the open preview.
patterns: Async action: `run` from a click → `await fetch(...)` → set value outputs → `Outputs.Success()`; wire Success onward for sequencing.
Transform between nodes: array in, reshaped array out, feeding a Repeater.
Shared helper: `exports.canStep = …` in `scripts/engine/rules.js`, `engine/rules.js` under Uses on each Function that needs it, and `Scripts.rules.canStep(tile)` in each body.
antiPatterns: Wiring to the bare script name — `toProperty: "amount"` for a script reading `Inputs.amount`. The port is `in-amount`; the bare name is only its display label, and the mistake survives every validator to fail on the canvas.
Rebuilding what a dedicated node already does (querying cloud data, navigation) — you lose live updates and editor insight.
Relying on auto-run while also connecting `run`; once `run` is connected, only the signal executes the script.
Pasting the same helper into several Functions. The copies drift apart; put the helper in a script file and list it under Uses.
Reading `Noodl`, `window` or `document` inside a script file. They're `undefined` there, so do that work in the Function and pass the values in.
